name: BJU Press Math
line: BJU Press Math is a course of lessons for each grade. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review happen at every problem.
description: AMP vs BJU Press Math: BJU teaches a set course of lessons for each grade. In AMP, assessment, teaching and review are continuous, at every problem.
verdict: BJU Press Math is a course for each grade, taught lesson by lesson on a schedule, by a teacher on video or by a parent from the teacher's edition [1][3][4]. In AMP, assessment and teaching are continuous. Every answer updates the learner's level and sets the next problem, and each problem carries its own hint, lesson and worked answer.

reasons.title: The problem is the unit
reasons.body: In AMP, everything a learner needs hangs off the problem in front of them: a hint that gives the first step, a lesson with a worked example, a video lesson, the worked answer afterward, and links to the skills it builds on and leads to. In BJU Press Math the unit is the lesson. In Math 5, a video lesson opens with a brief review, teaches the new idea, has the student try problems alone, then goes over them with the teacher. Assigned work follows [3]. In the textbook format, the parent teaches each lesson from the teacher's edition [1].

reasons.title: Continuous assessment
reasons.body: AMP has no separate test and no test day. It places a learner from their first answers, and every answer after updates the learner's level and sets the next problem: new work within reach, a gap to close, or an old skill due back. In BJU Press Math the family chooses a course for one grade, and the Homeschool Hub lays it out as a schedule of lessons [2][4]. The parent can skip, replace or reschedule lessons [4].

reasons.title: Feedback on every answer
reasons.body: After every answer, AMP shows whether it was right, the correct answer and the worked steps. In BJU Press Math the video teacher goes over the lesson's practice problems [3]. Online tests and quizzes grade themselves from grade 5 up, in the video and DVD formats [4]. The parent checks other work with answer keys [1][4]. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, of mixed ages and subjects, feedback that explains had the largest average effect [8].

reasons.title: Continuous review
reasons.body: In AMP, learned skills come back in ordinary practice, at growing intervals, mixed with other math. In BJU Press Math, each Math 5 video lesson opens with a brief review [3]. We found no schedule for returning to older skills in the course and Hub pages we read [3][4]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [7].

reasons.title: A level for each part of math
reasons.body: AMP keeps a separate level for each part of math, on one map of skills from counting through precalculus. A learner further along in one part than another gets work at both levels, and repeated misses send practice back to what a skill builds on. BJU Press Math is a separate course for each grade, from K5 through Precalculus [2].

reasons.title: Workbooks made for one learner
reasons.body: AMP makes printable workbooks for each learner from that learner's own record, with worked answer keys, and work done on paper counts. BJU Press Math prints student textbooks, teacher's editions, handouts and answer keys for each course, the same for every learner in it [1][4].

rows.range: K5 through Precalculus, one course per grade or subject, plus Consumer Math [2].
rows.start: The family chooses a course for one grade [2].
rows.teaching: A teacher on video, or the parent from the teacher's edition. A Math 5 lesson reviews, teaches, has the student try problems, then goes over them [1][3].
rows.next: The next lesson on the course schedule. The parent can skip, replace or reschedule lessons [4].
rows.mastery: None found in the pages we read [3][4].
rows.review: A brief review opens each Math 5 video lesson [3]. No schedule for older skills found in the pages we read [3][4].
rows.print: Student textbooks, teacher's editions, handouts and answer keys, the same for every learner in the course [1][4].
rows.adult: Runs the schedule, checks work with answer keys and keeps grades. In the textbook format, teaches each lesson from the teacher's edition [1][4].
rows.reports: A gradebook the parent can edit, with reports and transcripts. Online tests and quizzes grade themselves from grade 5 up, in video and DVD formats [4].
rows.evidence: No entry in Evidence for ESSA or the What Works Clearinghouse when checked [5][6].

theirs: BJU Press is a Christian publisher of textbooks for schools and homeschools. It describes its homeschool line as an all-in-one core curriculum, taught from a biblical worldview [1]. The math runs from K5 through Precalculus, one course per grade, with Fundamentals of Math, Pre-Algebra and Consumer Math along the way [2].

Each course comes as textbooks with a teacher's edition the parent teaches from, as a DVD kit, or as an online video course in the Homeschool Hub [1][4]. In Math 5, a video lesson opens with a brief review, teaches the new idea, has the student try problems alone, and then goes over them with the teacher. Assigned work follows [3]. The Hub shows the parent what is due, what is done and what materials are needed [4].
credit: A teacher on video for each lesson of its video courses, who works through the practice problems with the student [3].
A teacher's edition that gives the parent instructions, activities and added explanation for each lesson [1].
Hands-on manipulatives in the elementary grades [2].

theirs: We found no outcome study of BJU Press Math in the BJU Press pages we read, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [5][6].
ours: Two findings bear on this comparison. Across 40 studies of computer-based feedback, of mixed ages and subjects, feedback that explains averaged 0.49, against 0.32 for the correct answer alone and 0.05 for right or wrong only [8]. In a randomized trial with 787 seventh graders that meets What Works Clearinghouse standards without reservations, mixed and spaced practice scored 62% on the researchers' own test a month later, against 38% for practice in blocks [7]. AMP applies both at every problem.

AMP's own outcome studies are planned: growth on a national test against hours of use, then comparison groups, then randomized trials. Each will be registered before it starts and published whatever it finds. The research behind each part of AMP is in our report, and AMP is open source.

them: You want a teacher on video to teach each lesson, with a textbook beside it.
amp: You want assessment, teaching and review in the same practice, with no separate tests.
You want every answer checked and followed by the worked steps.
You want learned skills to keep coming back in practice.
Your child is at different levels in different parts of math.
You want workbooks made from your child's own record.

questions.question: How is AMP different from BJU Press Math?
questions.answer: BJU Press Math teaches a course for each grade, lesson by lesson on a schedule, by a teacher on video or by the parent [2][3][4]. AMP has no separate test: every answer sets the next problem, each problem carries its own teaching, and learned skills return in ordinary practice.

questions.question: Does BJU Press Math work?
questions.answer: We found no outcome study of BJU Press Math in the BJU Press pages we read, in Evidence for ESSA or in What Works Clearinghouse intervention reports [5][6].

questions.question: Can a learner use both?
questions.answer: Yes. AMP is a separate program. It places a learner from their first answers, whatever lesson they are on elsewhere.
